_doc: 1.8.0 (de-robotization slice 1, T2b, 2026-08-17) — the open mixes four
sizes from 3.0 to 4.5 around the shipped 4.0 (mean 3.975); the 3-bet
gains a 3.5 rung (mean 3.15 against a shipped 3.0). Seat-blind on
purpose: not adjusting to position is the archetype.
This is the widest open menu of the six, which is the point — a
recreational player picks a size by feel, and the spread is the cheapest
honest source of size variety on the table. It is also nearly
unobservable: 44 opens per 4,000 hands. The volume is recorded here so
nobody later reads the width as a measured effect.
The 3-bet rises rather than falls. A fish that raises at all tends to
raise big, and 3.5 is the vs-3-bet grading cap, so that is the ceiling.
The 3.0 open rung is inside `_STD_OPEN_CAP` and so makes a hero
three-bet against this seat gradeable, which no 4.0 open is.
[UNVERIFIED] — the weights, as for every pack in this ticket.
1.7.0 (de-robotization slice 1, T5, 2026-08-16) — postflop bet sizes are
re-weighted so this seat is no longer identifiable by size alone. The
realised bucket table for the whole roster is in the ticket ledger
(`docs/ai-dlc/ledger/phase3-derobotization.md`) rather than here — see the
tag's 1.8.0 entry for why.
It no longer shares a byte-identical sizing block with the calling station,
which was itself a tell: two personas that bet the same amounts are one
persona as far as a size read is concerned. This pack now spreads wider,
matching the RES-D bluff ordering that already places the fish above the
station.
Every value stays on the grader's recognised grid {0.33, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0,
1.5}; nothing is jittered continuously.
[UNVERIFIED] — no committed source in this repo gives a population
distribution of bet sizes at low-stakes full ring. See the calling
station's 1.7.0 entry for the one sourced observation this is anchored on.
1.6.0 (de-robotization slice 1, 2026-08-15, review rework) — `vs_rfi` is
answered per seat as three bands (big blind, small blind, everyone else), on
the same reasoning as the calling station. Facing a raise the fold runs 44.14%
in the big blind and 57.84% elsewhere, against a flat 56.41% before. The small
blind reads 57.83%, essentially the non-blind value, which is correct rather
than lazy: 0.5bb invested against 2.5bb to call, out of position, is not a
better price than a non-blind seat gets.
This pack is deliberately MORE price-elastic than the station — its big blind
continues 1.32x its baseline against the station's 1.17x — because price
elasticity is the fish's defining axis under the theory contract's P8, and an
earlier draft had authored it at the station's magnitude.
⚠️ The catch-all does NOT call; see the calling station entry for the F11
contract violation this removes. Range boundaries elsewhere are ramps: blocks
19% to 43% of the deck wide that played one way at weight 1.0 now play at
0.83-0.95 with adjacent bands outside them.
[UNVERIFIED] — fringe and per-seat weights have no committed source; they are
scaled to hold this pack's pre-slice measured rates.
